provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.title: Breach of voluntary undertaking
provisions.text: (5) Where a person fails to adhere to any term of the voluntary undertaking accepted by the Board, such breach shall be deemed to be breach of the provisions of this Act and the Board may, after giving such person an opportunity of being heard, proceed in accordance with the provisions of section 33.

provisions.title: Duties on receiving a correction request
provisions.text: (2) A Data Fiduciary shall, upon receiving a request for correction, completion or updating from a Data Principal,— (a) correct the inaccurate or misleading personal data; (b) complete the incomplete personal data; and (c) update the personal data.

negative

value.reason: The route `app.get('/api/Recycles/:id', recycles.getRecycleItem())` in server.ts has no authentication or ownership middleware, so it differs from the negative example that adds `security.appendUserId()`. The handler takes the record key straight from the request with `JSON.parse(req.params.id)` and runs `RecycleModel.findAll` filtered only by `id`. It never limits results to the caller's `UserId`. This matches the positive example. The Recycle model has `UserId` and `AddressId` columns, which link each record to a user and their address, so these are personal records. Any caller, even one who is not logged in, can change the id and read other users' recycle requests. This is a broken object-level authorization flaw (user-controlled key with no authorization). One gap: the evidence cuts off before the response is sent. But the `.then((Recycle) => {` callback follows the same pattern as the positive example, which returns the rows. The negative example's count and placeholder handlers return no row data, and nothing here suggests that.
